clue.text: Spot choice port reduced by 50 per cent

parts.note: a pick is a choice, as in 'take your pick'

indicators.note: reduced by 50 per cent means only the first half of the word for port is kept

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a harbour whose prices have been halved, looking for a bargain spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like a harbour or the wine, but here it is the nautical word for left, and halving it leaves LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a predicament or tight corner, just as being in a spot means being in trouble.

clue.text: Pressure group containing involuntary celibate and minor royal

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: containing says the word for group holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a ring is a group of people working together, often secretly
incel is the online contraction of involuntary celibate

explanation.surface: A lobbying body that includes an incel alongside a junior member of a royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A princeling is a young or petty prince, a royal of little importance or rank.

clue.text: Best getting Charlie to conceal parking offence

indicators.note: getting introduces the letter that comes into the word for best
to conceal says the new letter covers up and takes the place of the parking letter

parts.note: prime means best, as in prime cuts
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A top-rated person is told off by a policeman named Charlie for hiding an illegal parking violation.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie swaps in where P stood: PRIME becomes CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime is an offence against the law; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Contact hero saving regulars in cabins

indicators.note: saving is read as keeping something safe within, so the hero's word holds the picked letters

parts.note: a lion is a brave or celebrated person, a hero

indicators.note: regulars picks the evenly spaced letters, here the second, fourth and sixth of the word cabins

explanation.surface: Making contact with a hero who rescued the people staying in the cabins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' looks like rescuing, but here it means keeping safe inside; 'regulars' picks every other letter, starting from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a link or point of communication between people or groups, which is a contact.

clue.text: PCs struggling with old iron Stinger

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are thrown about and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the letters P, C and S

explanation.surface: Police constables wrestling with an antique iron get stung.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorpion is the arachnid with a venomous sting in its curled tail, so it is a stinger.

clue.text: Revolutionary tips from expert reduce noise from fans

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary

indicators.note: tips from takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A rebel's advice from a specialist on how to quieten down a cooling fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fans' looks like machines whose noise needs reducing; it means supporters, and their noise is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheer is the shout of encouragement supporters give their team, a typical noise from a crowd.

clue.text: Short broadcast about Lima favouring sweeping changes

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: radio is broadcasting, a broadcast medium
ca, from circa, means about
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A brief programme about the Peruvian capital promoting wholesale reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima looks like Peru's capital but supplies only its phonetic-alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical politician wants thorough reform of society at its roots, so favours far-reaching change.

clue.text: Love part of what a Roman inscription reflected

indicators.note: reflected says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a section of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of an ancient Roman inscription, seen in a mirror, turns out to be about love.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Love part' as the definition, but 'part of' is the signal that the answer lies within 'what a Roman inscription'; 'Love' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman with whom one is in love, a beloved or sweetheart.

clue.text: Stupid rocket launchers using nitrogen instead of sulphur

indicators.note: using brings in the replacement letter
instead of names the letter that is replaced

parts.note: NASA, the US space agency, launches rockets
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Rocket engineers being foolish by swapping one chemical for another in their fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a nana is a fool, so the word works as an adjective, stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a nana in British slang means they are silly or foolish.

clue.text: Head of permissive country has strippers in school?

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A liberal nation's leader whose academy employs exotic dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: these fish travel in schools and strip flesh from bones.
explanation.definitionFit: Piranhas are flesh-eating fish that swim in shoals and can strip a carcass to the bone.

clue.text: Copied one musical Rice sent to the West End?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in an across answer, going west means reading from right to left, so the words are turned round

parts.note: Evita is the musical by Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber
Tim Rice, the lyricist

explanation.surface: A Tim Rice musical transferring to London's theatre district, accused of being derivative.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district, a natural home for a Rice show; here 'West' means leftward, so the musical and lyricist's first name are read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imitative copies or mimics something else, so it is in effect copied.

clue.text: Milk daughter drops from great height

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
rain is water falling in drops from the clouds

explanation.surface: A daughter falls a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk' is a verb, meaning to exhaust or bleed dry.
explanation.definitionFit: To drain someone's money or energy is to milk it, using up resources until nothing remains.

clue.text: Wheels left behind collected by beloved French player

indicators.note: collected by says the French word gathers the other letters within it

parts.note: cher is French for dear or beloved
the seat is the behind, the backside
an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A French sweetheart picks up a footballer left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: A Chelsea tractor is British slang for a big four-by-four driven in posh city areas such as Chelsea in London; 'Wheels' is slang for a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheels is informal for a car, and this phrase is a mocking name for a large urban SUV.

clue.text: Provokes son outside of library without cause

parts.note: to needle someone is to provoke or goad them
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: outside of keeps only the outer letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up a boy outside the library for no reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something needlessly means doing it unnecessarily, with no good reason.

clue.text: Master list inscribed by king

indicators.note: inscribed by is read as having writing put within, so the king letter goes inside

parts.note: to list is to lean or tilt, as a ship does
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An expert's roster with a monarch's name written on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a catalogue; it is the verb for a ship tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a subject is to learn it thoroughly; the verbs share the sense of acquiring skill.

clue.text: Harmful titanium's impregnated plug

indicators.note: impregnated says one thing has got inside another, so the symbol goes into the word for harmful

parts.note: adverse means harmful, as in adverse effects
Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium; the 's means 'titanium has'

explanation.surface: A dangerous metal has soaked into a stopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like a stopper; it is the verb to promote.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a product is to promote it heavily, which is to advertise it.

clue.text: Put down drone 51 on isle inside of gates

indicators.note: on says the numeral follows directly after the island letter

parts.note: a drone is a low continuous hum
I is the map abbreviation for isle or island
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: inside of keeps the letters within the word, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: An unmanned aircraft brought down onto an island within some gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' suggests the aircraft, but it gives the low sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone down is to belittle or humiliate them, making them feel small.

clue.text: Cider and a lot of Moët disorientated pedestrian

indicators.note: disorientated means confused, so the letters are mixed up
a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: the champagne name, letters MOET

explanation.surface: Someone on foot who has drunk too much cider and champagne loses their bearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker; it is the adjective for dull and ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means uninspired and ordinary, which is what mediocre work is.

clue.text: Backward county hosting priest's made into a story

indicators.note: hosting says the reversed county takes the priest's name in as a guest
backward says the county is written in reverse

parts.note: Devon is an English county
Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible; with the 's

explanation.surface: A rural backwater county where a clergyman's life was turned into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' looks like a slur on the county but is the signal to write it in reverse: NOVED.
explanation.definitionFit: To novelise a film or event is to rewrite it as a novel, turning it into a narrative.

clue.text: Agile Newton developed conclusion of apple's descent

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for the newton, the unit of force

indicators.note: conclusion of takes the final letter of the word

parts.note: the fruit's name; the 's is possessive

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton, nimble of mind, formed his theory from where the apple ended up.
explanation.walkthrough: The apple's descent is the famous fall that inspired Newton; here descent means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is line of ancestry, family origin; descent has the same genealogical sense.

clue.text: Bear flag when leaving main road

indicators.note: leaving says those letters depart from the word for flag

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
in Britain an A road is a main road, so main gives A

explanation.surface: A bear carrying a flag wanders off the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the verb: to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it, as in 'I can't stand it'; bear has the same meaning.

clue.text: Secretly take long hollow sticks up on middle of field

indicators.note: on, in a down answer, places the reversed letters above the final piece
up, in a down answer, says the letters are read from bottom to top
hollow means emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: gums means sticks together with glue

indicators.note: middle of takes the centre letter of the word

explanation.surface: Long hollow sticks lifted in the middle of a field, like bamboo canes hiding contraband.
explanation.walkthrough: LG (hollow long) plus GUMS, read upwards, gives SMUGGL; the E from the middle of field goes beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To smuggle something is to carry it in or out covertly, particularly past customs or guards.

clue.text: Caring old queen arranged extravagant delivery

indicators.note: arranged says the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A kind, elderly monarch planned a lavish distribution of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' looks like a parcel being dropped off but means a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandiloquence is pompous, high-flown language, an over-elaborate style of speech or oratory.

clue.text: Still wearing English coat in restaurant

parts.note: in means wearing, as in 'in a hat'

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outermost layer, so only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone sits motionless while still in their coat at a restaurant table.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless or inactive, which is the adjective sense of still.

clue.text: Loop ring some way through part of mug

indicators.note: some way through says the ring sits partly into the word, inside it

parts.note: mug is slang for face, and the nose is a part of it
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A circle hangs part of the way down a drinking mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup; it is slang for face.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot that tightens when pulled.

clue.text: Smart city abandoning past

indicators.note: abandoning says the city leaves those letters behind

parts.note: Chicago is a US city
ago means in the past, as in 'years ago'

explanation.surface: A fashionable city turning its back on its history.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, as smart does when describing clothes or appearance.

clue.text: Provided area beyond centre of Thai city

indicators.note: beyond says the area letter comes after the rest
centre of takes the middle two letters of the word

parts.note: if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: Given land outside the middle of a Thai city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thai city' reads as one phrase, but the city is in Israel: Thai only gives its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Haifa is a major port city in northern Israel, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Rank for one American at rear of unnamed zone

indicators.note: at rear of puts the American letters at the end

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one

indicators.note: unnamed says the abbreviation for name, N, is taken out of the word

parts.note: a region is a zone or area
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: An American soldier's rank, for example, placed at the back of an anonymous sector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a military grade; it is the adjective meaning glaring or gross, as in rank stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means flagrant and outrageous, the sense of egregious in egregious error.

clue.text: Check island harbours shrimp

indicators.note: harbours means shelters within, so the island holds the other word

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
to vet something is to check it

explanation.surface: An inspection of a Greek island's harbours finds shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Crevette is French for prawn or shrimp and is used on menus in English too.

clue.text: Put right arm finally inside piping

indicators.note: inside says that letter goes within the word for piping

parts.note: a piping voice is a high, thin one, which is reedy

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Straightening an arm that has ended up stuck inside a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piping' looks like tubing; it is the adjective for a thin high sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy a fault is to correct or fix it, putting the situation back in order.
